topic: Setting up Claude Cowork properly once: a working folder, global instructions, handing over whole tasks, using less of your usage allowance, and a first 20 minutes
audience: People on a paid Claude plan who have tried Cowork a few times and want it set up so it does real work without constant hand-holding
goal: Make one working folder, write global instructions from a template, choose an approval mode, hand over one whole task, and know how to make the usage allowance last
notes: Anthropic describes Claude Cowork as bringing Claude Code's agentic capabilities to knowledge work beyond coding; it takes on complex, multi-step tasks instead of answering prompts one at a time. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

The intended workflow is: describe an outcome, step away, and come back to finished work such as formatted documents, organized files and synthesized research. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

When a task starts, Claude analyzes the request and makes a plan, breaks work into subtasks, runs code and shell commands in an isolated environment on Anthropic's servers, may run workstreams in parallel, and delivers outputs to the session. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]
Cowork can produce Excel spreadsheets with working formulas, PowerPoint presentations and formatted documents. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

In the new Claude experience, chat and Cowork are merged into a single conversation with no mode to choose; you have it if the message box no longer shows 'Chat' and 'Cowork' options. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]
Cowork is available only on paid plans: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]
Claude Desktop for macOS, Windows and Linux (beta) offers Cowork on all paid plans; the download page is claude.com/download. [https://claude.com/download]

To start a Cowork session: open Claude (web, desktop app or mobile app), select 'Cowork' in the message box, describe the task, then review Claude's approach and let it run. In the new Claude experience there is no 'Cowork' option: you describe the task in any conversation. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile]

Local file access needs the Claude Desktop app open and connected, even though sessions run in the cloud. Sessions keep running when the desktop app is closed or the computer is asleep, but tasks using local files need the desktop app open. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Work runs on Anthropic's servers in an isolated environment and sessions and files are saved to your Claude account, so work continues if you close your laptop. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

On desktop, Claude can read and write your local files directly, without manual uploads or downloads, but only in folders you have connected. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Your folders stay on your computer; when a cloud task needs a file Claude fetches a copy of just that file, and those copies are deleted when you delete the session. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile]

Deletion protection: Claude must get your explicit permission (an 'Allow' prompt) before permanently deleting any files. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Anthropic advises creating a dedicated working folder for Claude instead of granting broad access, and keeping backups of important files. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

In the new experience, the folder where Cowork saved its work is shown as 'Storage folder' in Settings, and folders you gave Cowork access to are listed under 'Trusted folders'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]
Claude reads individual files up to 50 MB. [https://claude.com/docs/cowork/guide/projects]

If a connected folder is renamed or moved, Claude Desktop 6.6395.0+ on macOS 14+ can find it and ask to 'Keep connected'; on Windows, Linux or older macOS you must reconnect it. [https://claude.com/docs/cowork/guide/renamed-folders]

Global instructions are standing instructions applied to every Cowork session, for tone, output format or background on your role. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]
Set global instructions at Settings > Cowork, click 'Edit' next to Global instructions, type them and click 'Save'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

In the new Claude experience, Cowork Global instructions became part of 'Instructions for Claude' in Settings > Your Claude (Settings > Account in the older layout) and apply to every conversation. Account-wide Instructions are set in Settings > Your Claude > Instructions. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

Folder instructions add project-specific context when you select a local folder on desktop, and Claude can update them itself during a session. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]
Claude Desktop v5.1231.0 (10 November 2026) changed Cowork so edits Claude makes to a session's CLAUDE.md no longer update your global instructions. [https://claude.com/docs/cowork/changelog]
No source documents a size or character limit for Cowork global instructions. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Approval modes: 'Manually approve' (Manual), formerly 'Ask before acting': Claude pauses for Allow/Deny on actions. 'Automatically approve' (Auto): Claude keeps working and reviews each action for safety, blocking unsafe ones; if blocked repeatedly it switches back to asking. 'Skip all approvals' (Skip), formerly 'Act without asking': nothing checks Claude's actions; use only when you completely trust every action, connector, file and app involved. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

In the new experience Auto is rolling out as the default on Pro, Max, Ultra and Team; Manual is the default on Enterprise. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

Anthropic notes the Auto check can miss risky actions; for work involving money, messages sent as you or important files it suggests staying close or switching to Manual. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Switch to 'Manually approve' when a task touches sensitive files, accounts or sites, when using a new tool, plugin or site, or when mistakes would be hard to undo. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

Safety advice: watch for unexpected patterns (files or sites you didn't mention, scope creep) rather than validating every command, and stop the task if something feels off. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

You remain responsible for all actions Claude takes on your behalf, including messages sent, purchases, data modified and scheduled-task actions. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

Multi-step tasks (running code, creating files, using connected apps and the browser) use more usage than a quick question; each step uses tokens. The product FAQ says Cowork uses more of your rate limit because it coordinates multiple sub-agents and tool calls. No official page gives a number for how much more. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Official usage tips for Cowork: group related work into one task, start a new conversation for unrelated work, tell Claude when you only need a quick answer, and check Settings > Usage. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

All Claude surfaces (claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Desktop) draw on the same usage limit; paid plans have a 5-hour session limit and weekly limits. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

The five-hour period starts with your first message and resets in full five hours later; remaining usage is shown under 'Current session' in Settings > Usage. Weekly limits reset at a fixed day and time assigned to your account. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

Settings > Usage shows progress bars for the five-hour session and weekly limits on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

Factors that use limits faster include message length, attachment size, conversation length, tool use (Research, web search), model choice, effort level, artifacts and multi-step tasks. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]
Project content is cached and counts less against limits when reused; caches expire after inactivity. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

When a long chat nears the context limit, Claude automatically summarizes earlier messages; this uses more of your usage limit. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

Effort levels in the app are Low, Medium, High, Extra high and Max; higher effort takes longer and uses more of your limits. In the Claude apps the default effort is Medium. To change the model, click the model name next to the send button. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]

Anthropic positions Sonnet 5.5 as strongest at well-scoped everyday tasks and creating polished documents, slides and spreadsheets, while Opus 5.5 is for complex work needing careful judgment; Haiku 5.5 is built for high-volume work. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5]

Usage credits let Pro, Max and Ultra users keep working after hitting limits at standard API rates; they are enabled in Settings > Usage with a monthly spend limit. 'Reset for free' in Settings > Usage restores a five-hour, weekly or Fable limit. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-manage-usage-credits-for-paid-claude-plans]

Cowork projects group related tasks into workspaces with their own files, context, instructions and memory. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14116274-organize-your-tasks-with-projects-in-claude-cowork]

Type /schedule in any Cowork task, or click 'Scheduled' in the left sidebar, to create and manage scheduled tasks; safety advice is to start simple and review outputs after each run. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork]
Cowork sessions can't be shared with others, though individual artifacts can be shared. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Claude can hallucinate incorrect or misleading information; Anthropic says to scrutinize high-stakes advice and check cited sources. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8525154-claude-is-providing-incorrect-or-misleading-responses-what-s-going-on]

Voice mode is a beta feature on all plans (Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise) in Claude Mobile, Claude Desktop and the web, built to work best from a phone, with hands-free and push-to-talk modes; voice conversations count toward your regular usage limits. On the web and Claude Desktop, click the sound wave symbol in the lower right corner of the chat window to start; Claude stays in voice mode until you click 'Stop'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11101966-use-voice-mode]

Dictation converts your speech to text so you can type prompts by speaking; voice mode is a full two-way conversation. In the new Claude experience, voice mode works in any conversation, including ones where Claude is working on a task. In Claude Cowork and Claude Code, dictation is available but voice mode isn't. You can switch between text and voice in the same conversation and the context carries over. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11101966-use-voice-mode]

Claude Desktop for Linux is in beta (Ubuntu and Debian); Cowork is available there, but dictation is not available in this release and computer use is not yet available on Linux. [https://claude.com/download]

Claude Desktop system requirements: macOS 13 (Ventura) or higher, Windows 10 or higher, or Linux Ubuntu 22.04 LTS+ / Debian 12+ on x64 or arm64. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10065433-install-claude-desktop]

Approval mode selector: you can change the mode at any time from the mode selector in the chat box. In the new Claude experience, the permission setting in the message box offers Auto and Manual; if you last chose Manual in a browser or app, new conversations there keep starting in Manual. On Team and Enterprise plans, your admin controls whether 'Automatically approve' is available; if it is turned off, the mode doesn't appear in the selector. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

To approve a specific connector tool yourself (for example one that sends email), set it to 'Always ask': on the web or in Claude Desktop go to Customize > Connectors, select the connector and open the Permissions tab. Claude is built to ask before each use of that tool in every mode. 'Always ask' is rolling out gradually; on Team and Enterprise your organization's settings come first. You control which connectors Claude can use via the '+' menu in the chat box or Customize > Connectors. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

During a Cowork task: progress indicators show what Claude is doing at each step; Claude surfaces its reasoning and approach; you can jump in to course-correct or give more direction mid-task; you can open the same session on another surface to monitor progress, answer Claude's questions or redirect the work; for complex tasks Claude may coordinate several sub-agents at once. Tasks can run for extended periods. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Cowork usage tips, as worded in the help center: group related work into one task instead of several; start a new conversation for unrelated work, so Claude isn't carrying extra context; tell Claude when you only need a quick answer, not a file or finished deliverable; check your usage in Settings > Usage. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Cowork projects: find Projects in the left navigation panel and click '+'. The three ways to create one are 'Start from scratch', 'Import from project' and 'Use an existing folder'. With 'Use an existing folder' you pick a folder, then name the project, choose where to save it, add instructions, attach any extra files and click 'Create'. Each project has its own Instructions, Scheduled tasks, Context (a local folder, a linked chat project or a URL) and Memory. Projects in Cowork need the latest Claude Desktop. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14116274-organize-your-tasks-with-projects-in-claude-cowork]

Starting a session inside a Cowork project opens it with that project's folders mounted and its instructions applied; files Claude creates land in the project's folders, and what Claude learns is saved to the project's memory for next time. [https://claude.com/docs/cowork/guide/projects]

The 10 November 2026 changelog entry reads: 'Changed Cowork so that edits Claude makes to a session's CLAUDE.md no longer update your global instructions. To change them, use Settings.' [https://claude.com/docs/cowork/changelog]

Renamed or moved folder prompt: it shows the folder's new location first, then its old location. 'Keep connected' lets Claude use the new location in that session (permission to delete files doesn't carry over); 'Not now' leaves the session without the folder. If you don't answer within 10 minutes the prompt closes. Claude can rename and move folders inside the folders you connect; if you didn't move it and didn't ask Claude to, click 'Not now'. [https://claude.com/docs/cowork/guide/renamed-folders]

Instructions for Claude (account-wide Instructions): click your initials in the lower left corner, select Settings, then Your Claude ('Account' in the older Settings layout). Under 'Instructions', describe your preferred approaches or methods, common terms or concepts you use, typical scenarios you encounter and general communication instructions. They apply to all your conversations; project instructions apply only within that project. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features]

Settings sections named in Anthropic's help pages: General and Privacy [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile]; Your Claude [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features]; Capabilities [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them]; Usage [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]; Billing [https://claude.com/pricing]; Cowork [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork].

Memory in Cowork: in cloud sessions Claude starts from what it remembers from your chats, and what comes up in a Cowork task carries back to chat. To run a task without memory, turn 'Memory' off in the '+' menu before sending the first message; it can't be changed later. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Anthropic's usage tips: plan conversations (combine related questions in one message and give background up front), be specific and concise, batch similar requests into one message, and review your prompt before sending to avoid follow-ups. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices] In a long chat that triggers automatic context management, start a new conversation if you're near your limit; keep project instructions short, remove project files you no longer use, and use a lower effort level for routine tasks. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

To change effort in the Claude apps, click the model name next to the send button, click 'Effort', then choose a level; Low and Medium suit routine tasks and stretch usage further, while higher effort uses more tokens. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]
Weekly limits apply across all models; your next weekly reset time is shown in Settings > Usage. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

To turn on usage credits on Pro, Max or Ultra: Settings > Usage, click the toggle in the 'Usage credits' section, use 'Adjust limit' to set a monthly spend limit (or 'Set to unlimited'), then 'Buy usage credits', choose an amount and click 'Continue'. Usage credits are charged separately from the subscription; when work switches to credits, the limit warning changes to 'Now using credits'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-manage-usage-credits-for-paid-claude-plans]

A limit reset ('Reset for free' in Settings > Usage on web, desktop and mobile) restores a five-hour, weekly or Fable limit; it can't be undone once used, weekly limits still reset on their usual day and time, and an unused reset is lost if you downgrade or cancel. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17007452-what-is-a-limit-reset]

Anthropic's prompting guidance: treat Claude like a brilliant but new employee who lacks context on your norms and workflows; the key test is to show your prompt to a colleague with minimal context and ask whether they could follow it; give the reason behind an instruction; tell Claude what to do rather than what not to do. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices]

Examples are one of the most reliable ways to steer format, tone and structure. For Claude app users, Anthropic advises starting with one example and adding more only if the output still doesn't match, noting that Claude pays very close attention to details in examples. Longer, more complex prompts are not always better; the first prompt rarely works perfectly, so test and refine. [https://claude.com/resources/articles/best-practices-for-prompt-engineering]

Giving Claude explicit permission to say 'I don't know' can drastically reduce false information, according to Anthropic. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations]

Cowork can work with Word (.docx, .doc), PDF, .txt, .md, .html, .json, .csv, .tsv, Excel (.xlsx, .xls, .xlsm), PowerPoint (.pptx, .ppt), common images, YAML/XML/TOML and Jupyter notebooks, per the product page. [https://claude.com/product/cowork]

Tools and connectors are token-intensive: Anthropic suggests turning off connected apps a chat doesn't need and asking Claude not to search the web when you don't need current information. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

Memory is enabled for Cowork projects: Claude can remember context from tasks in a project and apply it to future tasks in the same project, and what Claude learns in one project doesn't carry over to other projects. A project also shares memory with your chats outside projects unless you turn off 'Use account memory'. Project sharing ('Can view' or 'Can edit') is available on Team and Enterprise plans. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14116274-organize-your-tasks-with-projects-in-claude-cowork]
